title: Language Models Share a Readout Bottleneck in Working Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.21176v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) reproduce a human working-memory signature on the N-back task: performance declines as memory load N increases, and errors concentrate on lures, items that repeat the current stimulus at a neighboring but incorrect serial position. We ask whether this shared behavioral signature reflects a shared mechanism. The literature offers two candidate accounts. On a precision account, softmax attention cannot concentrate its weight on the item N positions back, so adjacent items are retrieved instead. On an interference account, attention selects the correct item, but the content of competing items corrupts the decision. We dissociate these accounts in 15 pretrained LLMs from three families (70 million to 14 billion parameters) and in minimal transformers trained from scratch. In all three families, the attention heads that carry the task attend to the target on most missed matches. Linear probes decode near-perfect

translated_title: 语言模型在工作记忆中共享一个“读出瓶颈”
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）在N-back任务上复现了人类工作记忆的特征：随着记忆负载N的增加，性能下降，且错误集中在“诱饵项”上——即在相邻但不正确的序列位置重复当前刺激的项目。我们探究这种共同的行为特征是否反映了共同的机制。文献提供了两种候选解释：在“精度解释”中，softmax注意力无法将权重集中于N个位置之前的项目，因此检索到的是相邻项目；在“干扰解释”中，注意力已正确选中目标项目，但竞争项目的内容破坏了后续决策。我们在来自三个系列的15个预训练LLM（参数量从7000万到140亿）以及从头训练的极简transformer中对这两种解释进行了区分。在所有三个系列中，承担该任务的注意力头在大多数未命中的匹配上其实都注意到了目标项目；线性探针能够近乎完美地解码出相关信息。
tldr: 该论文发现，语言模型与人类共享同一工作记忆失败机制——错误并非源于注意力定位不准（精度不足），而是正确的目标信息在“读出”阶段受到干扰，即语言模型存在一个共同的工作记忆读出瓶颈。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that LLMs share with humans a working-memory readout bottleneck: attention correctly localizes the target item, but errors arise from interference at the readout stage rather than from imprecise attention.
